reader.decision: Apply the 200 MB limits now in pinewood.conf (scoped to /api/files) and settings.py, ship before Friday 30 October, and plan presigned upload as the later primary after 9 November.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows two 10 MB limits block every drawing, the config-only fix needs no frontend release and meets the 30 October deadline, while the presigned alternative cannot ship before 9 November and would miss Halvorsen's 2 November yard review.

reconstruction.problem: Halvorsen Marine drawings (60-180 MB) fail to upload because nginx has client_max_body_size 10m (deploy/nginx/pinewood.conf:8) and Flask has MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH of 10 MB (app/settings.py:3).
reconstruction.what_breaks: nginx returns 413 before the request reaches pinewood-app (logged for 94371840 and 167772160 byte uploads on 2026-10-27). Raising only nginx would just move the 413 to Flask. Halvorsen cannot meet its Monday 2 November yard review.
reconstruction.fix: Keep 10m server-wide in nginx, add location = /api/files with client_max_body_size 200m (proxying to pinewood-app:8000) above location /api/, and set MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH to 200 * 1024 * 1024 in settings.py. No frontend change needed.
reconstruction.cost: Flask's limit is global, so any Flask route accepts 200 MB bodies, though nginx still blocks other /api/ routes at 10m. The two limits must be kept in sync across two files. Slow uploads hold an nginx buffer slot but not a gunicorn worker. Temp disk use is at most about 4.5 GB/day on a 20 GB volume. Presigned upload is deferred until after 9 November because there is no frontend release before then.

follow_up_questions: Is there any other proxy, load balancer or CDN in front of nginx with its own body-size limit that would still reject 200 MB?
Does the /api/files location need any other headers or settings that the existing location /api/ block provides, which the new exact-match block would drop?
Is the nginx timeout (proxy_read_timeout and client_body_timeout) enough for the ~72 second slow-uplink upload?
reader.closing_answer: Apply the 200 MB limits in pinewood.conf (scoped to /api/files) and settings.py now. Do not wait for the presigned upload, which can follow after 9 November if files grow beyond 200 MB.
